# APIVerve Documentation

> APIVerve publishes 388 ready-to-call APIs behind one key and one response shape. Every API answers with the same three top-level keys (`status`, `error`, `data`), authenticates with an `x-api-key` header, and is billed per call.

Markdown source for the guide pages below is available at the same path under https://docs.apiverve.com/md/, e.g. `/md/quickstart.md`.

Reference pages have no /md/ mirror of their own: each one canonicalises to its APIVerve catalog page, and it is that page which carries the markdown mirror worth quoting. Both are linked per entry below.

## Start

- [Quickstart](https://docs.apiverve.com/quickstart): Get a working API call in about four minutes. The same request shape works on every endpoint in the catalog.
- [Making requests](https://docs.apiverve.com/making-requests): Query parameters, JSON bodies, file uploads, timeouts and concurrency — everything that works the same way on every endpoint.

## Guides

- [Hide your API key behind a proxy](https://docs.apiverve.com/guides/hide-your-api-key): A key in front-end code is readable by everyone who loads the page. Two working proxies — Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge — plus what to do when the key genuinely has to be public.
- [Migrations](https://docs.apiverve.com/migrations): Moving an existing integration onto APIVerve — the order to do it in, what actually changes in your code, and how to cut over without a flag day.
- [Migrating from RapidAPI](https://docs.apiverve.com/migrations/rapidapi): Replacing per-API hosts, keys and subscriptions with one host and one key — the code changes, the mapping problem, and cutting over safely.

## Reference

- [All endpoints](https://docs.apiverve.com/api-endpoints): The full catalog — every endpoint, what it costs per call, and a reference page with parameters, response fields and a live sample for each one.
- [Response format](https://docs.apiverve.com/response-formats): The three-key envelope every endpoint returns, the five formats it can be serialised as, and why premium fields are absent rather than null.
- [Analytics API](https://docs.apiverve.com/analytics-api): Read your plan, credit balance, renewal date and usage breakdown programmatically — from an endpoint that never spends a credit.
- [Batch requests](https://docs.apiverve.com/batch-requests): Run up to 200 lookups for one endpoint in a single call, with one authentication, one rate-limit charge and one billing settlement.
- [CORS](https://docs.apiverve.com/cors): Calling the API directly from browser JavaScript — what is allowed, what fetch can read back, and why a missing key looks like a network error.

## Platform

- [SDKs and libraries](https://docs.apiverve.com/sdk): One generated package per API in seven ecosystems, plus a CLI — what exists, what it is called, what it does for you, and when calling the endpoint directly is the better choice.
- [MCP server](https://docs.apiverve.com/vervekit/mcp): Connect the whole catalog to an agent as native MCP tools — hosted, OAuth or key auth, with input and output schemas so results come back structured.
- [GraphQL](https://docs.apiverve.com/graphql): One POST that calls several APIs at once and returns only the fields you asked for — what it costs, what it will not do, and when REST is still the better call. Alpha.
- [Writing queries](https://docs.apiverve.com/graphql/usage): Query syntax, arguments, calling several APIs in one request, the explorer, and handling GraphQL-shaped errors code by code.
- [Mock endpoints](https://docs.apiverve.com/vervekit/mock): Stand up fake API responses on your own mock server — fixed bodies, status codes, headers and request rules — before the real thing exists.
- [Embedded forms](https://docs.apiverve.com/vervekit/forms): Drop a working form for any endpoint onto your site with two lines of HTML — no backend, no key in the browser.
- [APIVerve Studio](https://docs.apiverve.com/studio): The desktop API client — what it does, how it differs from the browser playground, and where your requests are stored.

## Integrations

- [Integrations](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations): Connecting APIVerve to automation platforms — which ones have a built connector, what they all share, and what an integration call costs.
- [Zapier](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/zapier): Using any APIVerve endpoint as a Zap action — connecting, dynamic fields, output mapping, and the failure modes worth knowing.
- [Make](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/make): The APIVerve module in Make — connecting, pre-filled parameters, and using routers, iterators and error handlers around an API call.
- [Vercel AI SDK](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/vercel-ai-sdk): Giving an AI SDK model APIVerve tools — the six ready-made tools, and reaching the rest of the catalog with findApis and runApi.
- [Node-RED](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/node-red): Installing the APIVerve node from the palette, setting the key, and calling any API from a flow with msg.payload.
- [Coda](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/coda): Adding the APIVerve Pack to a Coda doc, connecting your key, and pulling any API into a table with formulas and column formats.
- [Airtable](https://docs.apiverve.com/integrations/airtable): Adding the APIVerve extension to an Airtable base, signing in, and filling columns from any API in one run.

## Product tour

- [AI Assistant](https://docs.apiverve.com/dashboard/ai-assistant): Ask for a code snippet, an endpoint recommendation or help debugging an integration — and what the alpha's message and token limits mean.
